title: Cosmic Birefringence in CMB Polarization
bottleneck: Several analyses find a ~0.3-degree rotation of CMB polarization (cosmic birefringence), hinting at parity-violating physics like axion-like fields coupled to photons. The signal hovers near systematic limits of polarization-angle calibration, and independent confirmation is lacking. An axion-like field coupling to photons is the leading explanation, which would connect the signal to dark matter or dark energy physics.
why_it_blocks: A confirmed rotation would be the first cosmological evidence of parity violation beyond the Standard Model. Even a marginal signal motivates better calibration, since the payoff of a confirmed detection would be enormous.
current_state: Planck PR4 analyses report ~3 sigma; absolute angle calibration from Crab Nebula and future CMB-S4 data will decide. Improved absolute calibration using artificial sources and better foreground modeling are the priorities.
